hooks.description: Block dangerous shell commands that could damage the project or hardware

hooks.prompt: Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a KNOWLEDGE EDITOR (updating domain reference material, hardware docs, API references). If you are NOT in a knowledge editor role (e.g. you are an engineer, grader, tester, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this knowledge accuracy review only applies to knowledge editor sessions. If you ARE the knowledge editor, proceed: Review this file change for Zephyr knowledge accuracy. If the file is NOT a Zephyr reference file (.md in a skills directory), respond {"ok": true} immediately. For Zephyr reference files, check: 1) API signatures match current Zephyr v3.x documentation. 2) Devicetree examples use proper syntax (node-name@unit-address format). 3) Kconfig symbols follow CONFIG_ prefix convention. 4) No deprecated APIs referenced without migration notes. Respond {"ok": true} if accurate, or {"ok": false, "reason": "specific inaccuracy"}.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved creating or modifying knowledge reference files (markdown files in skills directories). If NO knowledge reference files were created or modified in this session, respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to knowledge authoring sessions. If knowledge files WERE modified, check: 1) New or modified reference files contain substantive content (not stubs). 2) Code examples in reference files compile conceptually (correct Zephyr API usage). 3) No TODO/FIXME markers left in reference content. Respond {"ok": true} if complete, or {"ok": false, "reason": "specific issue"}.
